slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: AST transfers an amino group from aspartate to α-ketoglutarate, forming glutamate and oxaloacetate.
Oxaloacetate is reduced to malate by malate dehydrogenase (MDH) with NADH; the rate of NADH decrease, measured at 340 nm, is proportional to AST activity.
AST is highest in heart muscle, liver and skeletal muscle cells; it is used with ALT and ALP in liver disease and to follow patients after myocardial infarction.

slides.title: Principle and source
bullets: This protocol follows, as an example, the instructions for use of the SPINREACT “GOT (AST)-LQ” kit (IFU BEIS46-I, 02/11/22). The IFU of your laboratory’s own kit always takes precedence: other kits may use different volumes, times, factors and reference values.

slides.title: Specimen, reagents and equipment
bullets: Specimen: serum or plasma — stable 7 days at 2–8 °C.
R1 (buffer): TRIS pH 7.8 80 mmol/L, LDH 800 U/L, MDH 600 U/L, L-aspartate 200 mmol/L.
R2 (substrate): NADH 0.18 mmol/L, α-ketoglutarate 12 mmol/L.
Equipment: spectrophotometer or analyser reading at 340 nm, 25/30/37 °C thermostat (± 0.1 °C), 1.0 cm cuvettes.

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: Working reagent: 4 volumes of R1 (buffer) + 1 volume of R2 (substrate).
Working reagent stability: 21 days at 2–8 °C or 72 hours at room temperature (15–25 °C).
Signs of deterioration: particles, turbidity or blank absorbance at 340 nm < 1.00 (NADH broken down).

slides.title: Reagent preparation (for a semi-automatic analyser)
bullets: The values come from the SPINREACT “GOT (AST)-LQ” IFU (BEIS46-I). The IFU of the kit you use and the analyser manual always take precedence — check the programme against them.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 1. Conditions: wavelength 340 nm; constant temperature 25 °C, 30 °C or 37 °C (thermostat ± 0.1 °C).
2. Use a 1 cm cuvette; zero the instrument with distilled water or air.
3. Pipette into a cuvette: working reagent 1.0 mL + sample 100 µL.
4. Mix and wait 1 minute.

slides.title: Procedure (manual, per the IFU)
bullets: 5. Read the initial absorbance (A), start the stopwatch and read every 1 minute for 3 minutes.
6. Calculate the absorbance differences and the mean change per minute (ΔA/min).

slides.title: Semi-automatic analyser: AST programme
rows: Initial A, then every 1 min for 3 min

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: AST (U/L) = ΔA/min × 1750.
Temperature conversion (IFU table): result at 25 °C × 2.08 = 37 °C; at 30 °C × 1.54 = 37 °C.
Linear up to 467 U/L; above that, dilute the sample 1/10 with NaCl 9 g/L and multiply the result by 10.

slides.title: Calculation and result
bullets: IFU reference (37 °C): men up to 38 U/L, women up to 31 U/L (19/16 at 25 °C, 26/22 at 30 °C).
These values are for orientation; each laboratory should establish its own reference range.

slides.title: Interferences and errors
bullets: Haemolysis interferes.
Heparin, EDTA, oxalate and fluoride do not affect the results.
Keep temperature and timing exact; the reference range must match the measuring temperature.
Drugs and other interfering substances are listed in the literature (IFU — Young DS).
IFU: performance depends on the analyser used.

slides.title: Quality control
bullets: Assayed control sera are run with each series (IFU: SPINTROL H Normal and Pathologic).
If a control falls outside its range, check the instrument, reagents and technique; do not release patient results.
Each laboratory sets its own quality-control scheme and the corrective actions when controls are out of tolerance.

slides.title: Safety
bullets: The reagent contains sodium azide, which can form explosive azides in lead and copper plumbing — flush with large volumes of water when disposing.
Serum and plasma are potentially infectious: wear gloves and never pipette by mouth.
Follow the precautions in the IFU and the safety data sheet (SDS) when handling the reagents.
Used cuvettes, tubes and tips are disinfected.
